title: 12 BMW Motorcycles Worth Every Penny - Top Speed
content: In the American motorcycle market, BMW Motorrad offers one of the most diverse lineups of bikes. These range from luxury tourers to do-it-all adventure bikes to retro-vibing roadsters and track-going monsters. At the same time, BMW surprisingly keeps the value quotient in check (particularly from a European bikemaker context), and most of its bikes are worth each penny you pay. We're talking about 12 such bikes, ranging from touring bikes with Japanese reliability to adventure bikes that excel at everything. There's something for everyone here. BMW offers the best of two-wheeled luxury, comfort, and performance with the K 1600 GTL. This full dresser brings the best of "big" American luxury charm with sophisticated technology to offer a surprisingly versatile land yacht. A unique six-cylinder engine powers the K 1600 GTL. This 1,649 cc mill produces 160 horsepower at 6,750 RPM and 132.7 pound-feet at 5,250 RPM. Power is sent to the rear wheel via a six-speed manual coupled to a final shaft drive system. For the chassis, a cast-aluminum bridge-type frame is present. It is suspended on BMW's famed Duolever front suspension with a central spring strut and 4.5 inches of travel. The rear gets the Paralever setup, coupled to a cast-iron single-sided swingarm and 5.3 inches of travel. Technology features are galore, too. Notable ones include a huge 10.25-inch TFT, a four-button cluster for custom functions, dynamic traction control, three ride modes, dynamic electronic suspension, hill start control, heated grips and seats, and an audio system, among others. This is arguably the most value-packed luxury touring motorcycle, and it undercuts the Honda Gold Wing, despite being more powerful. The 1,649 cc mill mentioned above is present here as well, in the same exact tune. Power is sent to the rear wheel via a six-speed manual and a final shaft drive neatly hidden in its single-sided swingarm. The chassis is also similar to the GTL, featuring the bridge-type cast aluminum frame. As for suspension, the front gets a double-wishbone (Duolever) with 4.5 inches of travel. The rear gets a monoshock (Paralever) setup with 5.3 inches of travel. The suspension offers electronic adjustability and even an automatic load-leveling feature. There is no dearth of top-spec technology. The K 1600 B gets a huge 10.25-inch TFT with a wide range of connectivity and integrated map navigation features. Other notable features include three ride modes, dynamic traction control, hill start control, and engine brake control, among others. If you’d rather pick an old-school full-dress tourer than one of the new-age ones, then BMW’s R 18 Transcontinental is worth a look. Taking the fight straight to Harley-Davidson’s Grand American Tourers, this full-dress Beemer builds on the R 18 cruiser with every luxury touring essential you’ll ever need and then some. It makes for a first-class touring experience that will have you looking forward to every touring opportunity. It’s powered by a big boxer engine that delivers at least 110 pound-feet of torque between 2,000 and 4,000 RPM. Other touring bits include a relaxed riding posture, a massive fairing with deflectors, high-quality saddlebags and a topcase with available central locking, and available active cruise control. It also gets a large TFT display paired with 4 traditional analog gauges, with an available Marshall sound system. It’s a unique German take on a formula that’s otherwise very American. Also, the Pope has one! This futuristic-looking touring bike makes luxury feel practical. The same boxer twin powers the R 1300 RT as on the go-anywhere R 1300 GS. The 1,300 cc mill produces 145 horsepower at 7,750 RPM and 110 pound-feet of torque at 6,500 RPM, sent to the wheel via a six-speed manual gearbox coupled to a final Cardan shaft drive system for added durability. Underpinning the R 1300 RT is a two-part frame with the engine utilized as a stressed member. It is suspended on BMW's famed Telelever front and Paralever rear suspension setups with 5.8 inches of front and 6.2 inches of rear travel. Adding to its versatility is a factory-adjustable seat, solid wind protection, and commendable technology. Notable features include keyless ride, dynamic electronic stability control, heated grips, and a gorgeous-looking 10.25-inch TFT with Bluetooth navigation as standard. This BMW adventure bike is famed for being a flagship that can do it all exceptionally well. Powering the flagship GS is the 1,300 cc liquid-cooled mill, which produces 145 horsepower at 7,750 RPM and 110 pound-feet at 6,500 RPM. Power is sent to the rear wheel via a standard six-speed manual with a final Cardan shaft drive system. It can also be equipped with an optional automatic transmission. Underpinning the R 1300 GS is a sophisticated setup. It comprises a pressed-steel main frame utilizing the engine as a stressed member. It is suspended on a double-wishbone suspension setup up front with 7.5 inches of travel. The rear gets a link-type monoshock with 7.8 inches of travel. BMW has loaded the R 1300 GS to the brim with technology features. Notable ones include four ride modes, dynamic traction control, dynamic brake control, dynamic cruise control, and hill start control. The dashboard comprises a sizable 6.5-inch TFT. The BMW S 1000 RR is a surprisingly affordable sports bike that is cheaper than a Honda Fireblade. Powering the S 1000 RR is a proven inline-four engine that produces 205 horsepower at 13,000 RPM and 83 pound-feet of torque at 11,000 RPM. It is coupled to a WSBK-derived quick throttle as standard as part of its latest update. Underpinning the flagship BMW sportbike is a lightweight twin-spar aluminum frame, coupled to a race-derived aluminum swingarm and subframe. The frame is suspended on 45 mm inverted front forks with 4.7 inches of travel, alongside a monoshock with 4.6 inches of travel. Both ends offer full adjustability. Cutting-edge technology such as six ride modes, pit lane limiter, launch control, dynamic traction control, wheelie control, and slide control is present, too. This BMW crossover feels worth every dollar because it blends urban mobility, highway runs, and even spirited mountain sessions so seamlessly. The S 1000 XR packs a proper superbike engine derived from the S 1000 RR. The 999 cc liquid-cooled inline-four mill produces 170 horsepower at 11,000 RPM and 84 pound-feet of torque at 9,250 RPM. Power is sent to the rear wheel via a six-speed manual gearbox. Underpinnings comprise a bridge-type cast aluminum frame, using the engine as a load-bearer, suspended on long-travel springs. The front gets 45 mm inverted forks with 5.9 inches of travel, and the rear comprises a monoshock with 5.9 inches of travel. Its electronic, self-adjusting rebound settings at both ends instill sharp cornering confidence. Technology features are plentiful and stitch its do-it-all character together. This is BMW's arch-nemesis to the Triumph Scrambler 1200. The R 12 G/S is powered by a mighty 1,170 cc boxer twin engine with 109 horsepower at 7,000 RPM and 85 pound-feet of torque at 6,500 RPM. Power is sent to the rear wheel via a six-speed manual gearbox coupled to a final Cardan shaft drive system for added durability. The engine sits in a tubular space frame and is suspended on long-travel suspension. The front gets 45 mm inverted forks with 8.2 inches of travel, and the rear gets a monoshock with 7.8 inches of travel. Both ends are fully adjustable. This is further complemented by durable aluminum cross-spoke wheels wrapped with all-terrain tires. The R 12 G/S gets a slew of assistive technology features. Notable ones include riding modes, dynamic traction control, cornering ABS, dynamic engine brake control, and partial integral brake system. This classic cruiser bike matches the essence of American big twins but with a unique twist: a large air-oil-cooled boxer-twin engine instead of a V-twin. In fact, it is the largest production motorcycle flat twin until the much-anticipated production-spec R 20 breaks cover. The 1,802 cc mill produces 91 horsepower at 4,750 RPM and 120 pound-feet of torque at 3,000 RPM. Adding to its heavy-duty outlook is a double-loop steel main frame with bolted beams. A twin-sided steel swing arm is part of the chassis and adds to its stretched-out stance. The R 18 gets telescopic forks up front with 4.7 inches of travel. The rear comprises a hidden monoshock that seems to be strongly inspired by the Harley Softail series. Owing to its old-school charm, BMW has added very little technology to the R 18, with notable features being LED lighting and a USB Type-C port only. This is a gravely overlooked BMW naked bike that offers grin-worthy performance at a bargain price. It is powered by the same 999 cc inline-four liquid-cooled engine as the S 1000 RR, but subtracts the ShiftCam for a more peaky output of 170 horsepower at 11,000 RPM and 84 pound-feet of torque at 9,250 RPM. Power is sent to the rear wheel via a six-speed manual gearbox coupled to a standard slipper clutch. The chassis components are also S 1000 RR derived, featuring inverted 45 mm forks up front with full adjustability and 4.7 inches of travel and a fully adjustable monoshock with 4.6 inches of travel. With a curb weight of as low as 432.1 pounds, the power-to-weight ratio is commendable on this Beamer. The S 1000 R is further tamed with a slew of top-spec electronics, such as M Quick action throttle, engine drag torque control, and three riding modes. title: Karol G SoFi Stadium Guide: Outfits, Merch, Setlist - LAmag
content: Close out the summer by attending the ‘Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour’ at SoFi Stadium this weekend Latin Grammy winner and singing sensation Karol G will be making her way to Los Angeles this weekend for three nights at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood for the hottest tour of the summer: Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour. Fans in attendance can expect the weekend of Aug. 14 to Aug. 16 to be filled with musical infusions of reggaetón, Latin pop and musica urbana as she performs her Tropicoqueta album along with some of her greatest hits. As her L.A. shows begin to creep around the corner, some may need a little help getting prepared for the big nights ahead. Here is your go-to guide for the perfect night: dress code, what to listen to and where to buy merch. Fit in with the Tropicoqueta aesthetic by wearing all things orange, pink, sparkles and maybe even some denim. Since we’re still in the summer season, fans can rely on their tropical summer attire by wearing vibrant colors to stand out amongst the crowd. Stores such as Pacsun, Urban Outfitters and Free People can make for great options when putting together a last-minute look. Consider a pair of comfy shoes to prepare for the long night of dancing and singing. Don’t forget the walk to and from the car. Karol G x Reebok is the perfect reference. Look at the selections of comfy yet stylish shoe options and see what best suits you and your concert attire. With the tour having started in late July, fans are now able to research socials and look for the official tour setlist to study. Ticketmaster has a few of the official songs in their ‘tour information’ section of their page that are a guaranteed part of the show. Look up some of her biggest hits such as LATINA FOREVA, Tusa, Mi ex tenía razón and MAMIII, just to name a few. Keep in mind that setlists are subject to change on a night-to-night basis depending on location. L.A. fans may be in for a special feature of her newest album, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto. On Aug. 7, followers were surprised by her newest project that features artists such as Bruno Mars and Drake. The artist included a fully English track along with a tribute to the late Tejano singer, Selena Quintanilla. Cash App and Karol G are partnering up to bring the Tropicoqueta tour to life through an immersive fan pop-up experience. Fans from the five selected cities of Los Angeles, El Paso, New York, Miami and Dallas can visit the first retail activation starting in L.A. The attraction features exclusive merchandise, limited edition finds and song lyric installations. As fans move through each attraction, they’ll receive a collectable stamp that makes their experience one of a kind. “I’m so excited for my fans to step inside the world of ‘Viajando Por El Mundo’ and feel like they’re traveling through all the beautiful places I imagined when I made the song,” Karol G. said. Fans will receive 20% off their purchase when paying with a Cash App Card. A free slushie will also be included with a merch purchase depending on location. title: Will GS's Push Into Options-Based ETFs Enhance Its Competitive Edge? - TradingView
content: The banking industry is witnessing a structural shift toward active ETFs and options-based income products, as investors increasingly seek higher income, tax efficiency and downside-risk management within the liquid ETF wrapper. Derivative-income ETFs have grown to roughly $180 billion in assets, seeing a CAGR of more than 70% since 2021, according to Goldman's official press release citing Morningstar. Against this backdrop, The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. GS has agreed to acquire NEOS Investments for consideration of up to $2.25 billion in cash and equity, subject to certain performance and service commitments. The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, pending regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions. The acquisition will add $30 billion in assets across NEOS' 19 options-based income ETFs to Goldman Sachs Asset Management's existing $40 billion in income and outcome-oriented options-based ETF solutions. Once complete, the deal will make Goldman Sachs Asset Management the eighth-largest active ETF provider. The NEOS purchase follows Goldman's acquisition of Innovator Capital Management, and together the deals create a broad options-based ETF franchise spanning buffer, managed outcome and income strategies. As of June 30, 2026, Goldman Sachs Asset Management, Innovator from Goldman Sachs Asset Management and NEOS manage more than $130 billion in ETF assets under supervision. Overall, Goldman Sachs’ push into options-based ETFs is likely to enhance its competitive advantage by giving the firm greater scale, a broader range of differentiated products and stronger exposure to fast-growing active ETF categories. The addition of NEOS, alongside Innovator, strengthens Goldman’s presence across income, buffer and managed-outcome strategies, helping it compete more effectively for investor assets. At the same time, the expansion should support higher recurring fee revenues and further diversify its Asset & Wealth Management business. Competition has been intensifying for Goldman as banks like Morgan Stanley MS and JPMorgan JPM are expanding crypto-related capabilities even if they have not yet launched proprietary ETFs. Morgan Stanley has filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to launch ETFs linked to Bitcoin and Solana. The proposed products — the Morgan Stanley Bitcoin Trust and the Morgan Stanley Solana Trust — are designed to give investors direct price exposure to the two cryptocurrencies without requiring them to own or store the tokens themselves. JPMorgan has taken a broader, infrastructure-led approach to crypto and blockchain. The bank offers crypto trading services to institutional clients and has built out custody capabilities, while also piloting on-chain settlement and tokenized deposits through its blockchain unit, Onyx. JPMorgan has launched blockchain-based platforms for wholesale payments and repo transactions, enabling faster and more efficient settlement using tokenized assets. GS shares have jumped 38.8% in the past year compared with the industry’s growth of 26.3%. From a valuation standpoint, Goldman trades at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 14.61X, above the industry’s average of 14.25X. title: State Department expands push to reclassify employees as at-will workers - Government Executive
content:
The State Department is expanding its search for employees to reclassify as at-will workers under the Trump administration’s new Schedule Policy/Career designation
                  
                    J. David Ake/Getty Images The State Department is taking another look at its workforce to see if more employees should fall under a new governmentwide designation that makes them easier to fire. Agency officials are expanding their search for employees to reclassify as at-will workers under the Trump administration’s new Schedule Policy/Career designation for the federal workforce. President Donald Trump signed an executive order in June that officially reclassified 8,000 federal employees into Schedule Policy/Career, a rebranding of the Schedule F designation that Trump pursued in his first term, but did not implement before leaving office. Employees placed into the new schedule would no longer be able to challenge adverse personnel actions before the Merit Systems Protection Board, and whistleblower complaints filed by Schedule P/C employees would be investigated by their own agency, rather than the Office of Special Counsel. The Office of Personnel Management previously estimated that about 50,000 federal employees would fall under this new job category. But an OPM spokesperson said in June that the administration chose to instead focus on “the most senior-level career policy officials.” The State Department’s actions suggest that its initial reclassification of employees fell short of the White House’s expectations, and other agencies may take a similar approach. NOTUS first reported that the Trump administration is directing agencies to find more federal employees to convert to Schedule P/C. A spokesperson for the foreign policy agency declined to comment on “internal deliberative personnel matters.” One State Department employee told Government Executive that human resources officials are using a short questionnaire to determine if GS-13 and GS-14 level employees are working in policymaking positions that should be reclassified to Schedule P/C. “It is not clear how many ‘yes’ responses would trigger a new Schedule P/C status,” the employee said. The questionnaire asks if a position “formulates, develops and/or determines foreign policy, including creation of draft documents with policy recommendations," or "develops or reviews non-public Executive Orders, regulations, directives, policy memoranda, or deliberative materials protected by the deliberative process privilege regarding foreign policy." Other screening questions ask if an employee “provides substantive advocacy of foreign policy,” or represents the department before Congress, the Office of Management and Budget, foreign governments or external organizations regarding the administration’s foreign policy. The questionnaire asks if an employee “publicly advocates Administration foreign policy through official communications or media engagement” or “exercises delegated authority to commit or bind the Department to policy decisions." The department is also looking for positions that conduct official bargaining or negotiations on behalf of the department, or whether an employee “performs statutory policy-making responsibilities." The State Department has already shifted supervisory foreign affairs officers and specialists, as well as other senior-level positions, to Schedule Policy/Career. A second State staffer said the department is still in the early stages of its expanded search for Schedule P/C conversions, but added that this work is “moving relatively fast.” Staff have been directed to update to their position descriptions to ensure they reflect the full scope of their responsibilities. “GS-13s, I don’t think, are typically in a position that you’re going to think of as a senior policymaking position,” the employee said. “I was surprised, personally, to see positions that junior given this designation.” A senior administration official told reporters in June that 97% of employees that fall under Schedule Policy/Career are at a GS-15 level or higher. The official said a “small number” of GS-13 and GS-14 employees were also converted, but that most of them work at OMB. “Outside of OMB, there are very, very few positions that are below the level of GS-15 that are being covered,” the administration official said. “The bottom line is that almost all of these are very senior positions in the federal government.” The administration official said Schedule Policy/Career would “increase the accountability of officials who are responsible for carrying out the elected president’s policy agenda,” but would have little day-to-day impact on reclassified employees. “As long as they’re performing their job duties in a competent, professional manner, they have nothing to be afraid of,” the official said. The second State Department employee said Schedule P/C’s impact on the workforce has not yet been fully felt, but suggested that newly at-will employees may be reluctant to offer candid feedback on policy matters. “If you convert my position to a position that can be expeditiously removed, I’m going to more carefully tailor what I’m saying,” they said. “Its practical effect, I think it’s safe to assume, is that it will reduce people’s willingness to give advice or offer policy positions that are inconsistent with the direction of the administration.” A third individual said the department has started reviewing GS-13 and GS-14 positions for “possible conversion to Schedule Policy/Career.” “That process has resulted in a hold on reclassifying any of the thousands of GS-13 and 14 positions, which an office or bureau might otherwise do from time to time to align position grades with updated responsibilities,” the individual said. OPM's guidance to agencies states that many aspects of federal employment – including rules around pay, leave, benefits and reductions in force – remain unchanged for those moved to Schedule P/C. OPM also included a sample termination notice agencies may use when firing Schedule P/C employees. In the template, agencies may specify “unacceptable performance or misconduct” as justification for an employee's termination. title: Bespin Global’s AI Platform Wins Grade 1 GS Certification - thelec.net
content: The “HelpNow Agentic AI Platform v4.0,” an artificial intelligence (AI) agent platform developed by AI services and solutions company Bespin Global, has received Grade 1 Good Software (GS) certification from the Telecommunications Technology Association (TTA). ​Bespin Global plans to use the certification to strengthen its public-sector business. It supports inference, tool integration, workflow execution, application programming interface (API) integration, and external-service calls based on the Model Context Protocol (MCP). ​Bespin Global also said the product can minimize hallucinations in generative AI and improve the accuracy and reliability of responses through its proprietary agentic retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), few-shot training, and dynamic-prompt technologies. ​The HelpNow Agentic AI Platform has also obtained ISO/IEC 42001 certification, an international standard for artificial intelligence management systems, and has been adopted by organizations including the National Pension Service, the Ulsan Metropolitan Office of Education, and the Ministry of the Interior and Safety’s “Modu-ui Gwangjang” platform.

title: SGA Solutions Becomes First in South Korea to Earn GS Certification for ICAM Solution - finance.biggo.com
content: SGA Solutions (CEO Choi Young-chul), a comprehensive IT security firm, announced on the 13th that its zero trust-based integrated identity, credential, and access management (ICAM) solution, 'SGA ZTA ICAM,' has become the first ICAM solution in South Korea to receive GS (Good Software) certification. GS certification is a nationally accredited quality certification system that comprehensively evaluates software functionality, reliability, usability, and other attributes. With this certification, SGA ZTA ICAM has been objectively recognized as meeting the software quality standards required by public institutions and various industry sectors. ICAM is a security solution that verifies who users are and centrally manages which systems they can access and with what privileges. As the adoption of generative AI and agentic AI accelerates, companies must now manage not only user accounts but also a rapidly growing number of non-human identities (NHI), including service accounts and API accounts. As AI agent utilization expands, the number of digital accounts and access privileges requiring management within enterprises grows correspondingly, making ICAM—which centrally manages and continuously verifies both user and non-human account privileges—increasingly critical in zero trust environments. title: South Korea's National Pension Service Surpasses 10% Stake in GS E&C, Becoming Largest Single Shareholder Ahead of Founding Family - finance.biggo.com
content: The National Pension Service (NPS) has raised its stake in GS Engineering & Construction (006360.KS) above 10%, firmly cementing its status as the largest single shareholder. As GS Group's founding family continues to sell down its holdings, the NPS's growing presence is creating subtle tension in the corporate governance structure. According to the Financial Supervisory Service's electronic disclosure system on the 13th, the NPS currently holds 8,576,383 shares, representing a 10.02% stake in GS E&C. The fund purchased an additional 598,434 shares on the open market on the 6th, adding to its existing 7,977,949 shares. The average acquisition price was 27,932 won (approximately $19.73) per share, with the total purchase amounting to approximately 16.7 billion won (approximately $11.8 million). GS E&C maintains a governance structure in which GS Group's founding family and related parties divide their shareholdings. The combined stake centered on Chairman Huh Chang-soo reaches 23.02%, but on a single-shareholder basis, the NPS holds the largest position. With this latest open-market purchase, the NPS has widened its gap over Chairman Huh Chang-soo (5.95%), the largest individual shareholder, to 4.07 percentage points. The situation was different just a few years ago. In 2023, Chairman Huh Chang-soo was the undisputed largest shareholder with an 8.28% stake in GS E&C, exceeding the NPS's 8.05% holding. However, after Chairman Huh gifted 2 million shares to his eldest son, CEO Huh Yoon-hong (3.89%), his stake fell to 5.95%. During that period, the NPS steadily accumulated shares on the open market, widening the gap. The founding family's diminishing control is also evident in share sales. In April, Huh Dong-soo, honorary chairman of GS Caltex, Huh Se-hong, vice chairman of GS Caltex, and Huh Doo-hong each sold their entire holdings of GS E&C shares—15,000, 10,000, and 21,429 shares, respectively. This reduced the list of controlling family members in GS E&C to 13, including Chairman Huh Chang-soo. Earlier in March, Huh Jung-soo, chairman of GS Neotek, sold 358,158 shares, bringing his stake down to 1.09%, while Huh Chul-hong, CEO of GS Entec, sold 130,000 shares, roughly half of his holdings. These sales are interpreted as profit-taking. GS E&C's stock price fell to an intraday low of 12,670 won (approximately $8.95) in 2023, hovered around 20,000 won (approximately $14.13), then rose sharply in March-April this year. The share sales are estimated to have generated approximately 11.4 billion won (approximately $8.1 million) for Chairman Huh Jung-soo, 4.6 billion won (approximately $3.2 million) for CEO Huh Chul-hong, 500 million won (approximately $353,162) for Honorary Chairman Huh Dong-soo, 400 million won (approximately $282,530) for Vice Chairman Huh Se-hong, and 800 million won (approximately $565,060) for Huh Doo-hong. The NPS's expansion of its GS E&C stake is driven by expectations for the AI data center business. GS E&C, together with its subsidiary Xi C&A, is pursuing hyperscale AI data center projects in Goyang and Paju in Gyeonggi Province, as well as in Sejong. On the 10th, the company signed a memorandum of understanding with LS Electric for the supply of power equipment for AI data centers and related technology development, expanding its value chain. GS Group's broader vision for massive AI infrastructure is also a factor. The group is pursuing the construction of a 2.4-gigawatt (GW) AI data center within the Bukpyeong Second General Industrial Complex in Donghae, Gangwon Province, by 2029. GS E&C is expected to play a key role in this project, which involves an investment of approximately 30 trillion won (approximately $21.2 billion). Stable growth in the core business is another investment consideration. In the construction capability assessment released by South Korea's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport late last month, GS E&C ranked third domestically with an evaluation amount of 11.07 trillion won (approximately $7.8 billion), behind Samsung C&T (028260.KS) and Hyundai E&C (000720.KS). Cumulative new orders in the first half of this year reached 7.47 trillion won (approximately $5.3 billion), achieving more than 90% of the annual target of 8 trillion won (approximately $5.7 billion). Strengthened dividend policy also played a role. Despite a 64.6% decline in consolidated net profit to 93.4 billion won (approximately $66.0 million) last year, GS E&C raised its dividend per share from 300 won (approximately $0.21) to 500 won (approximately $0.35). Total annual dividends increased by approximately 70%, from 25.5 billion won (approximately $18.0 million) to 42.4 billion won (approximately $29.9 million). The NPS is selectively increasing its positions within the construction sector. In the second quarter, it raised its stake in DL E&C (375500.KS) from 9.32% to 10.45% and in Samsung E&A (028050.KS) from 7.31% to 8.34%. Its stake in HD Hyundai Industrial Development (052300.KS) also edged up from 10.08% to 10.13%. In contrast, the NPS reduced its Hyundai E&C stake from 10.23% at the end of March to 9.93% on April 24. This is interpreted as a portfolio adjustment favoring companies with order competitiveness and profitability in their own development projects. Second-quarter earnings were somewhat weak. GS E&C's consolidated revenue for Q2 was 2.78 trillion won (approximately $2.0 billion), with operating profit of 91.4 billion won (approximately $64.6 million), down 13.0% and 43.6% year-over-year, respectively. However, new orders surged 61.7% to 5.22 trillion won (approximately $3.7 billion), driven by a significant increase in secured construction rights for urban redevelopment projects. Since redevelopment projects take time from groundbreaking to revenue recognition, order volume does not immediately translate into profit. Securities analysts expect differentiation among construction stocks to intensify in the second half. Huh Jae-joon, an analyst at Samsung Securities, noted that "the construction industry in the second half faces a mix of positive factors—expanding order momentum—and negative factors—earnings uncertainty." A construction analyst at another securities firm commented, "Since it takes time for orders to translate into actual profit, it is difficult to conclude that earnings recovery is assured based on order volume alone," adding that "in the second half, construction companies' earnings and stock performance will diverge significantly depending on groundbreaking speed, cost ratio management, and sales performance." title: Bespin Global's HelpNow Earns Top-Tier South Korean GS Certification - finance.biggo.com
content: AI services and solutions company Bespin Global announced on the 13th that its enterprise AI agent platform, HelpNow Agentic AI Platform v4.0, has received Grade 1 GS (Good Software) certification administered by South Korea's Telecommunications Technology Association (TTA). GS certification is a nationally accredited software quality certification system designated by South Korea's Ministry of Science and ICT and operated by the TTA. It comprehensively evaluates overall software quality—including functional suitability, performance efficiency, usability, reliability, security, and compatibility—based on the ISO/IEC 25023 international standard. Grade 1 is awarded only to products that meet the highest level of quality conforming to international standards across all evaluation criteria. Products receiving Grade 1 certification can leverage it as a key requirement for entering the public procurement market, including designation for priority purchasing by public institutions, registration on the Public Procurement Service's KONEPS, and exemption from benchmark testing (BMT) in informatization projects. HelpNow is an integrated AI transformation (AX) platform for building, deploying, and operating enterprise AI agents based on generative AI. It supports multiple large language models (LLMs) with selectable options, along with reasoning, tool and application programming interface (API) integration, workflow execution, and external service invocation based on the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The platform enhances answer accuracy through retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), few-shot learning, and dynamic prompt technologies, and features a horizontally scalable architecture capable of running multiple AI agents simultaneously. The company noted that it has obtained ISO/IEC 42001 certification—the international standard for AI management systems—to manage risks in AI operations. HelpNow has already demonstrated tangible results across various industries including public, financial, and manufacturing sectors. South Korea's National Pension Service applied generative AI by integrating RAG knowledge management and LLMs with its existing chatbot to alleviate the workload burden on counselors caused by complex systems and regulations. As a result, consultation times were shortened, repetitive tasks were reduced, and data-driven consistent consultation quality was secured. South Korea's Ministry of the Interior and Safety built the public engagement platform "Everyone's Plaza" on HelpNow in just four days. By integrating LLMs, speech-to-text (STT), and optical character recognition (OCR) into AI agents to automate document summarization, proposal classification, keyword extraction, and responsible ministry recommendations, the platform processed 1.81 million citizen opinions in real time over two months, with 237 items incorporated into actual national policy agendas. The platform has also been applied to AI education services at the Ulsan Metropolitan Office of Education. Bespin Global plans to further solidify its position in the public market following this certification. Specifically, the company will pursue registration on the KONEPS integrated shopping mall and expand AI agent templates specialized for administrative, welfare, and safety sectors. Optimization for public cloud environments will also be pursued concurrently. Park Ki-chul, head of Bespin Global's HelpNow AI Development Division, said, "This Grade 1 GS certification signifies that HelpNow Agentic AI Platform's technology and quality have been officially verified through national standards." He added, "With demand for AI transformation surging in the public sector, we will position HelpNow as the standard AI platform for the public market and lead South Korea's public AI innovation." title: $2.25 Billion Bold Bet: Goldman Sachs (GS.US) Acquires NEOS, Reshaping the Crypto Options Landscape - Moomoo
content: To create a seamless experience and for website quality and improvement purposes, we use cookie technologies for verification and quality purposes, to personalize the content presented, and to provide advertising that may be of specific interest to you. Learn our Privacy Policy here. Goldman Sachs plans to acquire NEOS for up to $2.25 billion, gaining access to 19 ETFs and $30 billion in assets under management (AUM). This move strengthens its positioning in Bitcoin and Ethereum options income strategies, distinguishing it from traditional spot ETFs. According to Woofun AI, Goldman Sachs (GS.US) officially announced an acquisition agreement with NEOS on August 12, marking a strategic shift for the Wall Street giant from simple crypto asset custody to a complex options-based business platform. The core of this transaction is not merely acquiring a cryptocurrency fund, but rather integrating NEOS's mature options ecosystem to build a comprehensive yield-generation system covering both traditional financial assets and digital assets. As the agreement was made public, market focus quickly shifted from the transaction amount itself to how Goldman Sachs plans to combine its vast client base with NEOS's unique options yield strategies to open new growth curves in the increasingly competitive ETF market. The financial structure of the deal is highly conditional and incentive-driven, with the acquisition consideration capped at $2.25 billion. The payment method includes cash and equity, with portions directly linked to future performance targets and service commitments. This means that $2.25 billion represents a theoretical valuation peak rather than a fixed cost. Based on this maximum amount, the transaction's valuation multiple is approximately 7.5% of NEOS's current assets under management (AUM), a ratio that appears relatively restrained yet highly targeted within the context of financial M&A. Subject to approvals from regulators such as the SEC and other customary closing conditions, the transaction is expected to close formally in the first quarter of 2027. As a key component of the deal, NEOS co-founders Troy Kacz and Garrett Polera will be promoted to partners at Goldman Sachs Asset Management post-closing, ensuring the stability of the core strategy team. Data compiled by Woofun AI shows that NEOS currently manages 19 ETFs with total AUM of approximately $30 billion. The vast majority of these products employ active management strategies aimed at generating excess returns through options instruments. Notably, NEOS's largest products are not cryptocurrency-related funds, but rather its traditional market offerings: the S&P 500 High Income ETF (SPYI) and the Nasdaq-100 High Income ETF (QQQI). By the end of July, AUM for these two funds had surpassed $10 billion and $13 billion, respectively. The remaining product line broadly covers small-cap equities, international stocks, real estate, bonds, U.S. Treasury notes, hedging strategies, and leveraged yield products, forming a diversified traditional asset yield matrix. Beyond its traditional business, Goldman Sachs gains a series of cryptocurrency-related products with proven operational expertise through this acquisition, most notably the NEOS Bitcoin High Income ETF (BTCI). BTCI's AUM has reached approximately $1.1 billion, making it a leading product in its category. Additionally, NEOS manages the Boosted Bitcoin High Income ETF (XBCI) and the Ethereum High Income ETF (NEHI). XBCI is designed to achieve yield levels approximately 150% of those generated by BTCI's corresponding strategy, while NEHI employs a similar yield-oriented options strategy tailored to the Ethereum market. These products present a stark structural contrast to BlackRock's (BLK.US) iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT.US). IBIT adopts a simple trust structure to hold Bitcoin directly, aiming purely to reflect its price volatility, and charges a 0.25% custody fee. In contrast, BTCI takes a distinctly different path; its annual operating expense ratio is 0.99%, and it does not hold Bitcoin spot directly. Instead, it constructs exposure through complex derivatives operations. The prospectus filed by BTCI with the SEC explicitly states that its core objective is to generate substantial monthly cash income by selling options while maintaining exposure to Bitcoin's appreciation potential. Specifically, the fund constructs a synthetic covered call strategy by purchasing call options with similar strike prices and expiration dates and selling put options, thereby simulating price exposure without actually holding Bitcoin. This mechanism allows the fund to generate cash flow through the decay of options' time value and the collection of premiums when Bitcoin prices rise moderately or trade sideways. However, if Bitcoin prices surge significantly beyond the relevant strike prices, the sold call options will begin to erode the capital appreciation gains achieved through long-term investment. The SEC clearly defines this approach as a "synthetic covered call strategy," the essence of which is trading part of the upside potential for deterministic monthly cash flows. Actual performance data for BTCI reveals the risk-return trade-off inherent in this strategy. As of June 30, BTCI's annualized distribution rate stood at 26.16%, while its 30-day SEC yield for the same period was 2.13%. However, the attractive high monthly distributions mask severe volatility in net asset value (NAV). Data shows that as of June 30, BTCI's one-year NAV total return, adjusted for distributions, was -40.9%. Bloomberg data shared by Eric Balchunas on August 11 further confirmed that, even accounting for subsequent market fluctuations, the loss over the one-year period remained approximately 42.5%. Although the fund distributes substantial cash to investors on a monthly basis, it cannot avoid a significant erosion of the overall principal. NEOS explains that these distributions are classified as return of capital for tax purposes, and their composition may include option premiums, dividends, capital gains, and interest. While this tax treatment of return of capital may offer certain tax advantages to investors, such as lowering the cost basis of the stock and thereby affecting the amount of gain or loss recognized upon future sale, it also means that the ostensibly high distribution rate does not accurately reflect actual investment performance. For U.S. investors, understanding the erosive effect of return of capital on the cost basis is crucial, as it directly impacts final after-tax returns. Unlike spot ETFs, BTCI’s return structure focuses more on generating regular cash flows rather than fully tracking every price rebound of Bitcoin. When Bitcoin prices surge sharply, the upside potential forgone by BTCI through selling call options may far exceed the income generated from the option strategy, causing its performance to lag significantly behind the spot price. Conversely, in market environments where Bitcoin prices move sideways or rise moderately, the advantages of the option strategy become apparent; even if call options expire without significant price appreciation, the premiums generated provide important support to final returns. However, this does not mean that sideways movement guarantees profitability; option pricing, holding costs, and minor fluctuations in the underlying asset price still exert complex influences on fund performance. More critically, BTCI remains exposed to the risk of declining Bitcoin prices. Its Bitcoin-related exposure shrinks as the market falls, and the hedging effect provided by call options is limited. In the event of a sharp market correction, option premiums accumulated over months could be wiped out instantly. BTCI’s performance over the past year is a typical example of this downside risk materializing rapidly; while investors enjoy high distributions, they must bear the cost of significant principal erosion. Goldman Sachs’ acquisition of NEOS is a key step in deepening its layout of option-based income products, rather than an isolated event. Goldman Sachs has already accumulated extensive experience with GPIX and GPIQ ETFs, which combine exposure to S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 assets with actively managed call option strategies, demonstrating its ability to generate income through options in traditional markets. In April this year, Goldman Sachs completed the acquisition of Innovator Capital Management, acquiring 171 fixed-income ETFs and approximately $31 billion in assets under management, showcasing its strategic preference for rapidly expanding its ETF footprint through mergers and acquisitions. The acquisition of NEOS brings Goldman Sachs an additional 19 operating ETFs with approximately $30 billion in assets under management, along with a professional team possessing mature products and strategies. Compared to launching new products from scratch and gradually building scale, directly acquiring mature products allows for rapid capture of market share. Market trends indicate that asset managers are increasingly utilizing option instruments to combine traditional asset exposure with monthly income, fixed buffer mechanisms, and leverage effects. The focus of competition has shifted from lowest-cost index tracking to the design of higher value-added income structures. A similar trend has emerged in the cryptocurrency sector: BlackRock launched its own Bitcoin premium income ETF in June, while Goldman Sachs filed an application for its proprietary Bitcoin premium income ETF in April. NEOS provides Goldman Sachs with live Bitcoin and Ethereum income products that already have a certain asset scale, enabling immediate entry into this fast-growing market segment. The first wave of spot Bitcoin ETFs addressed a fundamental question: How can investors gain Bitcoin exposure through brokerage accounts? Products like BTCI raise a deeper question: What role should this Bitcoin exposure actually play? Options can convert volatility into cash distributions, limit investors’ upside participation during price rebounds, increase leverage, or create more specific income structures. Although the ticker symbols for these products still reference Bitcoin, investors are no longer simply purchasing Bitcoin exposure, which alters the due diligence requirements investors must fulfill. For option-based cryptocurrency ETFs, understanding how income is constituted, its tax implications, and potential downside risks is as important as understanding the underlying assets. Through this acquisition, Goldman Sachs has not only acquired products but also gained the authority to define the investment logic for this emerging asset class. Goldman Sachs noted that, combined with its previous acquisition of Innovator Capital Management, its global ETF AUM will rise to approximately $130 billion, positioning it as the eighth-largest active ETF manager globally. Bloomberg ETF analyst Eric Balchunas described this as a "surprising move," highlighting NEOS’s rapid growth since its establishment in 2022 and Goldman Sachs’ aggressive strategy of acquiring two specialized firms within a short period. Notably, this large-scale acquisition comes against the backdrop of Goldman Sachs’ recent adjustments to its crypto holdings. In the first quarter, Goldman Sachs reduced its disclosed positions in cryptocurrency ETFs, specifically by selling funds related to Ripple and Solana, while also lowering its exposure to Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs. Despite the reduction, the bank reported holding Bitcoin ETF assets worth over $700 million at the end of the quarter. This strategic shift from direct holdings to indirectly expanding influence through the acquisition of specialized management platforms marks a deeper evolution in the crypto-asset allocation logic of traditional financial giants. title: GS The Fresh launches Mucho Más Starlight wines to tap Korea’s daily drinkers - CHOSUNBIZ - Chosunbiz
content: The supermarket GS The Fresh, operated by GS Retail(27,800 won ▲ 1,050 3.93%), said on the 13th that on the 12th it unveiled two "Mucho Más Starlight" wines, red and white, for the first time in Korea. Mucho Más is a wine brand whose name in Spanish means "more" and "much more." It is known as a daily wine that emphasizes value for money and is currently sold in 65 countries worldwide. Cumulative sales have surpassed 20 million bottles. The newly released "Mucho Más Starlight Red" adds vanilla and spice flavors to fruit aromas such as blackberry, raspberry, and cherry. It emphasizes soft tannins and a smooth texture. The white product adds tropical fruit flavors to aromas of peach, apricot, and citrus, and is characterized by fresh acidity and a vanilla finish. Each of the two products is priced at 22,900 won. To mark the launch, GS The Fresh will sell them at a discount of 19,900 won through the 18th. GS The Fresh's wine sales rose 9.8% in 2024 from a year earlier and then increased 19.6% last year. In the first half of this year, they also grew 27.4% from a year earlier, widening annual growth. Targeting this demand, GS The Fresh sells an average of about 40 types of wine per store, and some locations with an expanded assortment carry up to about 100 types. It plans to continue expanding its wine lineup around daily wines with strong value for money and exclusive items. Jun Jae-hyeok, GS Retail processed daily goods team MD, said, "Recently, wine has shed its image as a drink enjoyed only on special days and is becoming an everyday purchase made while grocery shopping," and added, "We will continue to strengthen our wine competitiveness by offering a wide variety, from value-for-money wines that can be enjoyed casually in daily life to differentiated products." The biggest bullish argument is that The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (NYSE:GS) is building a more diversified and recurring asset-management business. NEOS gives Goldman exposure to income-oriented ETFs that are designed around options strategies. That could be attractive to investors looking for regular income and some downside protection, especially when market volatility remains elevated. Goldman said its asset and wealth management revenue rose 20% year over year to $4.6 billion in the second quarter, showing that this part of the business is already gaining momentum. The deal also builds on The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (NYSE:GS)'s $2 billion acquisition of Innovator Capital Management, which closed in April 2026. Innovator brought Goldman roughly $31 billion in assets across defined-outcome ETFs. Adding NEOS should take Goldman's active ETF assets to around $80 billion, giving it considerably more scale in a rapidly expanding market. For Goldman shareholders, the longer-term benefit is less dependence on investment banking and trading. Those businesses can be highly profitable but are tied to deal activity and market conditions. Asset management can provide a steadier stream of fee revenue. The concern is that The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (NYSE:GS) may be paying a fairly high price to accelerate its ETF ambitions. The $2.25 billion maximum price represents roughly 7.5% of NEOS' $30 billion in assets under management. Reuters' Breakingviews noted that this looks expensive compared with the amount of assets Goldman is acquiring. There is also no guarantee that NEOS' rapid growth will continue. Options-based income ETFs have become popular, but competition is increasing. If more asset managers launch similar products, fees could come under pressure, and the returns of some strategies may become less compelling. The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (NYSE:GS) also has to integrate NEOS while digesting its earlier Innovator acquisition. If the firm cannot generate sufficient organic inflows or cross-selling opportunities, the deal could take longer than expected to earn an attractive return. JPMorgan Chase & Co. (NYSE:JPM) is probably the most relevant comparison. Both firms are using their investment-management platforms to capitalize on the shift toward active ETFs rather than relying only on traditional mutual funds. JPMorgan entered the active ETF market earlier and has built a substantial franchise. The firm describes itself as the No. 1 global active ETF provider by assets under management, based on data as of the end of 2025. Its ETF business spans equity, fixed income, income, and other strategies. Goldman's approach is different. Rather than simply building a broad ETF lineup organically, it is using acquisitions to quickly add specialized capabilities. The Innovator and NEOS deals give Goldman expertise in defined-outcome, income, and options-based ETFs. That creates an interesting trade-off. JPMorgan has the advantage of an established active ETF platform, while Goldman is trying to close the gap through acquisitions. The strategy could work well if active ETFs continue taking market share. JPMorgan Chase & Co. title: CSM Switches to Aston Martin for Rest of GS Season - Sportscar365
content: CSM adds second entry for Houk, Ellahi for final three races; enters GT4 America for Indy… Czabok-Simpson Motorsport has made the switch from Porsche to Aston Martin GT4 machinery for the remainder of the IMSA Michelin Pilot Challenge season, while adding a second GS class entry in the process. The Indianapolis-based team, which has long been affiliated with running Porsches, will field two Aston Martin Vantage GT4 Evos beginning with next weekend’s round at Virginia International Raceway. While Gordon Scully and Morgan Burkhard will remain together in the No. 2 entry, Ayrton Houk as Ismaeel Ellahi will team up in the No. 3 Aston Martin for a three-race Pilot Challenge program. The shift to the British manufacturer is being billed as a “strategic move” according to a team statement, in order to get a jump start on the 2027 season. Sportscar365 understands CSM acquired one of Rebel Rock Racing’s Astons that it previously ran in the series. “Moving both cars to the Aston Martin now is an important step in our preparation for 2027,” said team co-owner Stephen Simpson. “It gives our engineers and drivers three race weekends to build a meaningful base of knowledge in Michelin Pilot Challenge conditions. “Ayrton has already tested with us several times and has consistently impressed the team with his pace, feedback and approach. “Ismaeel’s development in such a short period has been exceptional, and his CTMP victory showed that he is ready for this next challenge. “Gordon and Morgan give us the experience and continuity we need, so we believe these lineups create a very strong foundation for the rest of this season and for 2027.” Houk, 23, is additionally confirmed to also contest the Pirelli GT4 America season-ending rounds at Indianapolis Motor Speedway with CSM, with his co-driver yet to be announced. “The testing I have done with CSM gave me a real appreciation for how the team works and how committed everyone is to performance,” he said. “To now join the Michelin Pilot Challenge program for VIR, Indianapolis and Road Atlanta is a huge opportunity. “I am excited to share the No. 3 with Ismaeel, learn the Aston Martin quickly and contribute to the team’s preparation for 2027. “Adding the GT4 America finale at my home track in Indianapolis makes this four-race program even more special.” Ellahi, a 19-year-old American-Pakistani driver has been competing in VP Racing SportsCar Challenge competition, where he scored GSX class honors at Canadian Tire Motorsport Park in CSM’s first outing with the Aston Martin. “Two years ago, I was sim racing in my basement, and after only eight car races I am now preparing to make my Michelin Pilot Challenge debut,” he said. “Winning at CTMP was an unforgettable moment, but it also made me even more motivated for this next step. “I am grateful to CSM, my family, my partners and everyone who has helped me progress so quickly. “I am especially proud to represent my Pakistani heritage at this level, and I hope this opportunity shows other young drivers that there can be a path into professional motorsport even if they start in a simulator.” John Dagys is the founder and Editor-in-Chief of Sportscar365. title: Oscar De La Rosa Defends Karol G’s ‘Alguien Que Te Amaba’ and Calls on Tejano Fans to ‘Stop Hating’ - Tejano Nation
content: La Mafia frontman says the cumbia’s ’90s-inspired sound is introducing Tejano music to new generations—and urges fans to celebrate artists who are taking the genre around the world Tejano music icon Oscar De La Rosa, the longtime frontman of internationally recognized Tejano supergroup La Mafia, is speaking out in support of Karol G’s “Alguien Que Te Amaba,” a cumbia co-written by the Colombian superstar, legendary Tejano singer-songwriter Pete Astudillo, and acclaimed songwriter-producer Edgar Barrera. The song has sparked conversation among Tejano fans, particularly over its unmistakable connection to the sound and spirit of Tejano cumbia from the 1990s. While some listeners have embraced Karol G’s interpretation as an opportunity to introduce elements of Tejano music to a massive global audience, others have questioned comparisons to the music of Selena and debated whether contemporary artists are appropriately representing the genre. For De La Rosa, however, the conversation should be less about comparisons and more about celebration. In a video shared on social media, the “Un Millón De Rosas” singer directly addressed those criticizing the song and urged fans to listen with an open mind. “¿Cómo es que no les gusta esa canción? ¿Qué pasa con ustedes? ¿Qué le pasa a los haters?” Translated to English, De La Rosa asked, “How can you not like that song? What’s wrong with you? What’s wrong with the haters?” He went on to defend Karol G, Astudillo and Barrera for creating a song that he believes is helping expose audiences outside the traditional Tejano community to a sound that shaped an important era of the genre. “Thank you for recording this song, because it is opening the eyes and ears of many people who have not heard our music,” De La Rosa said. He specifically pointed to the production’s ’90s influence, saying the song has “a lot of the style of our music from the ’90s.” That connection is particularly significant coming from De La Rosa, whose career with La Mafia spans decades of Tejano music’s evolution. Founded in Houston in 1980, La Mafia helped push Tejano beyond its traditional regional boundaries and became one of the genre’s most internationally successful groups. The band’s extensive touring in Mexico and Latin America helped establish a larger audience for Texas-based Tejano and Tex-Mex music. One of De La Rosa’s strongest messages was directed at the tendency to compare every successful female artist working within Tejano or Tejano-influenced music to Selena. “Why is it that whenever a woman records a song, they always want to compare her to Selena?” De La Rosa said. “Stop that. Come on. Give other people the opportunity to live their dream.” His comments echo a sentiment increasingly being voiced throughout the Latin music community: Selena’s legacy is monumental, but honoring her does not require placing every new female artist in her shadow. In the accompanying social media caption, De La Rosa reinforced that message, writing that “Selena will always have her place. Karol is writing her own story.” That distinction is important in the discussion surrounding “Alguien Que Te Amaba.” Rather than attempting to recreate Selena’s career or identity, Karol G is drawing inspiration from a musical tradition and introducing elements of that sound to listeners who may never have discovered the Tejano music of the 1990s. And having Astudillo—a songwriter whose work is deeply connected to Selena’s musical legacy—help bridge that generation gap makes the collaboration even more significant. “Alguien Que Te Amaba” arrives at a moment when Karol G is continuing to expand her musical palette. The song appears on her 2026 album No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto, released August 7, a project that represents a more introspective and experimental direction for the Colombian superstar. The collaboration with Astudillo gives the song a direct connection to the Tejano tradition, while Barrera brings his extensive experience as one of the most prominent songwriters and producers in contemporary Latin music. For many longtime Tejano fans, the song’s appeal is its familiarity. Its rhythmic character and musical flavor can evoke the golden era of Tejano cumbia while being presented through the voice and creative vision of one of today’s biggest Latin artists. De La Rosa believes that crossover can benefit the entire genre. He also pointed to Mexican-American group Frontera as another example of artists taking regional Mexican sounds to new audiences and said those efforts should be celebrated rather than criticized. “We have to be proud that someone out there loves what we’re doing, loves what we have done,” De La Rosa said, adding that he believes Selena herself would have been proud to see the music reaching new audiences. De La Rosa’s comments also touch on a larger issue facing Tejano music: gatekeeping. For decades, Tejano has maintained a fiercely loyal fan base that has protected its history, sound and cultural identity. That passion has helped preserve the music through changing musical trends and generations. But there is a difference between preserving a genre and preventing it from evolving. When fans insist that Tejano must sound exactly as it did during its commercial peak, emerging artists can find themselves caught between honoring the music’s roots and creating something that reflects their own generation. That tension is especially important today as younger Tejano artists incorporate elements of regional Mexican, pop, urban, electronic and other contemporary sounds into their music. Rather than viewing those influences as a threat to Tejano, De La Rosa’s message suggests they can be viewed as another chapter in the genre’s ongoing story. “That’s the reason why Tejano music came to an end, because of you haters that don’t allow it to continue to grow and become world-known music again.” Whether one agrees completely with De La Rosa’s assessment of Tejano’s decline, his larger point is difficult to ignore: a genre cannot reach new audiences if its own community rejects every attempt to take it somewhere new. De La Rosa is uniquely positioned to make that argument. Born in Houston, Oscar De La Rosa is best known as the lead vocalist of La Mafia, the Grammy-winning group he helped establish in 1980 alongside his brother Leonardo Gonzales and keyboardist and accordionist Armando Lichtenberger Jr. La Mafia emerged from Houston’s Northside and developed a distinctive sound that blended Tejano, cumbia, pop and other Latin influences. The group eventually expanded its reach throughout Mexico, Latin America and beyond, helping demonstrate that a Texas-based Tejano act could build an international audience. The band’s achievements include Grammy and Latin Grammy recognition, along with numerous Tejano Music Awards and Premio Lo Nuestro honors. La Mafia remains active, with De La Rosa continuing as its lead vocalist. In other words, De La Rosa isn’t speaking about musical evolution from the sidelines. He spent his career helping evolve Tejano music himself. De La Rosa concluded his message with a plea for fans to change the way they approach new artists and new interpretations of Tejano music. “Give someone else a chance,” he said. “Stop what you’re doing. Stop hating.” That message may be the most important takeaway from the debate surrounding “Alguien Que Te Amaba.” Tejano music has a rich history worth protecting. Selena’s legacy deserves to be celebrated. Pete Astudillo’s contributions deserve recognition. The music of La Mafia and the artists who built the genre deserve their place in history. But the next generation deserves room to create, too. If Karol G’s “Alguien Que Te Amaba” introduces millions of listeners to the sound of Tejano cumbia, perhaps the question should not be whether it sounds exactly like the music of the past. Perhaps the better question is where those new listeners go next. If they discover Selena, Astudillo, La Mafia, David Lee Garza, Mazz, La Sombra, Emilio Navaira and the countless artists who helped build Tejano—and then discover today’s emerging Tejano artists—the genre gains something far more valuable than nostalgia. It gains new listeners, new artists and another generation. As De La Rosa put it in his social media message: “Music is not compared, it is celebrated.” And for a genre that has spent years fighting to remain visible, that may be exactly the attitude Tejano music needs to move forward. title: New owner begins converting Italian Carrefour stores to the “historic” GS brand - RetailDetail EU
content: NewPrinces Group, the food company that acquired Carrefour’s Italian operations last year, is preparing to rebrand the stores under a brand familiar to millions of Italians. The historic Italian supermarket brand GS, which disappeared after being acquired by Carrefour in 2000, is making a comeback. NewPrinces Group, the new owner of the Italian Carrefour stores, is reestablishing GS as the flagship brand for the group’s retail operations. The company recently unveiled the new logo, inspired by the old GS brand (notably a red circle, just like the GB brand that Carrefour acquired in Belgium during the same period). In the coming months, the company will begin the gradual renovation of its stores and the modernization of its network across all formats. This involves approximately 1,000 stores, including about 750 franchise stores. For NewPrinces, the return of GS is more than just a rebranding, the company emphasizes in a press release. The move is part of the group’s industrial strategy, which aims to integrate production, logistics, and distribution into a single supply chain model. The goal is to strengthen the connection with the end consumer through a recognizable brand rooted in the legacy of Italian retail. “The GS logo embodies an important history and a bond that has been built over time with millions of customers. That is why we have chosen to retain its most recognizable elements,” says NewPrinces Chairman Angelo Mastrolia. The Belgian brewer Alken-Maes, part of the Heineken Group, ended 2025 with a decline in revenue and a substantial net loss in a shrinking market. The company does not expect to return to growth until 2029. HelloFresh has once again reported a decline in revenue and the number of orders for the second quarter of 2026. The company says it is focusing on existing customers with high margins, but rising costs are also weighing on profits. Customers with electric cars can no longer park them in any of the 18 rooftop parking lots that Carrefour operates in Belgium. The retailer says this is a precautionary measure: electric cars are heavy and difficult to extinguish.

Neos specializes in systematic options-based income strategies, writing index option overlays on equity, fixed income and alternative exposures within a tax-efficient ETF structure. Its flagship funds include SPYI, the S&P 500 High Income ETF with about $11.3 billion in assets; QQQI, the Nasdaq-100 High Income ETF with about $13.9 billion; and IWMI, the Russell 2000 High Income ETF with about $1.1 billion. The derivative income ETF category has grown to about $180 billion in industry-wide assets, compounding at more than 70% annually since 2021, according to Morningstar data cited by Jefferies. content: The municipal bond (muni) market underperformed the Treasury market in July, as reignited Middle East tensions brought inflation pressures back to the forefront. A persistent new issue calendar, modest pullback in demand and stretched starting valuations placed additional pressure on the muni market, contributing to the relative underperformance. While a moderating June CPI print supported the Federal Reserve’s decision to hold rates steady at 3.50-3.75% at its July FOMC meeting, renewed supply shock inflation concerns drove risk premiums higher, particularly at the longer end of the curve. This shift in market sentiment coincided with a slowdown in muni demand, contributing to the underperformance for the month. Muni yields rose an average of 36 basis points (bp) in July. The difference between 1-year and 30-year muni yields steepened 15 bp to 194 bp. Muni/US Treasury ratios cheapened by 5/6/2%, ending July at 65/70/84% for 5/10/30 years. Source: Goldman Sachs Asset Management. Bloomberg.  As of July 31, 2026. Source: Goldman Sachs Asset Management. Bloomberg. As of July 31, 2026. The Bloomberg Muni Index declined 1.85% in July, while the Bloomberg Muni High Yield Index decreased by 1.51%. All credit ratings (AAA–BBB) saw negative performance within investment grade munis. Source: Goldman Sachs Asset Management. Bloomberg. As of July 31, 2026. Supply for the rest of the year should remain elevated given continued infrastructure needs. We expect demand to persist due to the August seasonal summer reinvestment, with attractive yields providing compelling entry points for investors. Muni/US Treasury ratios remain near fair value across the curve and credit spreads are close to their 5-year historical averages. We see opportunity to lock in attractive absolute yields amid the recent interest rate volatility. We anticipate headline-driven volatility to remain present, but a resilient underlying economy and healthy reserve balances continue to put municipalities in a strong position to navigate the path forward. July new issue supply amounted to $44 billion ($43 billion tax-exempt and $1 billion taxable). This was 20% lower than July 2025 volumes and 28% lower than June. Year-to-date, new issue volumes are on par with this time last year. Weekly new issuance volumes in July ranged from $8.7 billion to $13.4 billion. Notable deals included $2.4 billion Connecticut Aquarion Water Authority, $1.8 billion California State University, and $1.5 billion NYC Transitional Finance Authority. Source: Goldman Sachs Asset Management. The Bond Buyer, Barclays. As of July 31, 2026. July saw positive inflows for all four weeks, with the strongest demand during the first two weeks with $1.3 billion each week. There was a sharp drop-off in week three to $174 million due to outflows from long duration and high yield munis, but demand accelerated in the last week of July with inflows of $761 million. Overall, July experienced robust demand across both investment grade and intermediate duration munis. Year-to-date fund inflows have totaled $62 billion, with the majority of flows into investment grade and long duration munis. Source: Goldman Sachs Asset Management. Refinitiv. As of July 31, 2026. Investment grade and high yield spreads tightened 7 bp and 11 bp, respectively, finishing July at 87 bp and 172 bp. Within high yield, despite overall spread tightening, the increase in yields on the month led to negative returns across most sectors, with only the Electric sector posting positive returns, at 0.31% for the month. Education and Puerto Rico showed the largest negative returns, down 2.58% and 2.05%, respectively. Source: Goldman Sachs Asset Management, Bloomberg. As of July 31, 2026. title: LS ELECTRIC and GS E&C partner on AI data centres - Transformer Magazine
content: The partnership will develop next-generation DC distribution systems and supply switchgear, GIS and transformers for AI data centre projects South Korea, Seoul: LS ELECTRIC and GS Engineering & Construction (GS E&C) have signed a memorandum of understanding to jointly develop next-generation DC power distribution technologies for high-density AI data centres. The agreement responds to rising electricity demand from GPUs and other high-performance computing systems, which is increasing pressure on data centre operators to improve power efficiency and supply reliability. Under the partnership, the companies will work on DC distribution technologies aimed at reducing power conversion stages and associated energy losses. They also plan to hold regular technical exchanges and explore applications for future projects. The cooperation will extend to power infrastructure for GS E&C data centres. LS ELECTRIC plans to supply switchgear, gas-insulated switchgear (GIS) and ultra-high-voltage transformers as part of the electrical systems supporting these facilities. LS ELECTRIC is also developing a wider DC distribution portfolio that includes solid-state transformers, solid-state circuit breakers and energy storage systems. The company operates a factory in Cheonan using DC power distribution as a demonstration environment for the technology. For GS E&C, the collaboration combines its data centre engineering and construction capabilities with LS ELECTRIC’s power equipment and DC distribution technologies. The agreement reflects the growing impact of AI data centre expansion on power infrastructure, with switchgear, GIS, transformers, power conversion equipment and storage all becoming increasingly important as computing densities rise. title: CDS' WeeAI Platform Receives Top-Tier GS Certification - thelec.net
content: South Korean AI company CDS said its integrated AI platform, WeeAI v1.6.0, has received Grade 1 certification under the GS (Good Software) certification program from the Korea Testing & Research Institute (KTR). WeeAI allows users to access and compare more than 30 AI models from nine major providers within a single environment. Supported models include those from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, SpaceX (xAI), Perplexity, Mistral, Meta and Alibaba. According to CDS, one of the platform's key features is multi-model simultaneous response, which enables a single prompt to be submitted to as many as three AI models at the same time. Users can compare differences in reasoning, perspective, expression and information quality before selecting the response best suited to their needs. The company said the feature helps reduce dependence on any single AI model and allows organizations to choose different models depending on tasks such as planning, research, analysis, translation, education and content creation. CDS describes WeeAI as an AI orchestration and operations platform designed to centrally manage AI accounts, costs, permissions and security policies across an organization. A key component of the platform is its shared credit-based billing system. Rather than requiring individual users to maintain separate subscriptions for multiple AI services, WeeAI enables organizations to purchase a common pool of credits that are deducted based on actual usage. Administrators can allocate credits by organization, department, group or user, while also controlling access to specific AI models and functions, setting usage limits and monitoring consumption. The platform additionally supports the distribution of shared prompts and organization-specific templates. CDS said the usage-based model can reduce costs associated with uneven utilization, inactive accounts and duplicate subscriptions while providing data-driven budgeting. If paid credits are exhausted, users can continue working through supported free AI models. According to the company, WeeAI offers nine generative AI work environments, including AI chat, presentations, documents, spreadsheets, images, videos, music, code generation and drawing tools. The platform supports output formats commonly used by Korean public-sector and educational institutions, including HWPX, DOCX, PDF, PPTX and XLSX. The platform can be deployed in cloud, dedicated private cloud, on-premises or hybrid environments depending on an organization's security policies and IT infrastructure. CDS said WeeAI also includes personally identifiable information (PII) detection and protection functions, knowledge base and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) integration for incorporating internal organizational data into AI responses, and support for single sign-on (SSO) and organizational directory integration. Looking ahead, the company plans to add capabilities such as automatic AI model recommendation and routing based on task characteristics, credit usage forecasting and budget controls, institutional prompt asset management, integration with legal and public data sources, account lifecycle management and industry-specific AI agents. GS certification is South Korea's national software quality certification program. Under the Software Promotion Act, software is evaluated across multiple criteria, including functional suitability, performance efficiency, compatibility, usability, reliability, security, maintainability and portability.

title: Citroen Built A Rotary GS, Then Tried To Buy Them All Back And Crush Them - Carscoops
content:
One of just 847 GS Birotors is heading to auction, alongside the even rarer rotary prototype that started the whole adventure The 1970s rotary gold rush persuaded everyone from GM to Mercedes that pistons were old news. Citroen jumped aboard too, only to eventually decide its rotary GS was something it would rather forget. It even tried buying the cars back so it could destroy them. Related: Citroen’s Iconic 2CV Is Coming Back As A $17,000 EV Fortunately, some owners didn’t cooperate. One of the survivors is this 1973 GS Birotor being offered without reserve by Broad Arrow at The Quail Auction, where its $20,000 to $30,000 estimate makes it look suspiciously affordable among Monterey Car Week‘s seven-figure exotica. The regular GS was already wilfully unconventional, with slippery styling and Citroen’s famous hydropneumatic suspension. It was deservedly named European Car of the Year in 1971. But through Comotor, its rotary joint venture with Germany’s NSU, Citroen stuffed in a twin-rotor Wankel derived from the technology used in the NSU Ro 80. The 2.0-liter unit produced 105 hp (106 PS) and drove through a three-speed semi-automatic transmission. Unfortunately, the Birotor arrived just as the 1973 oil crisis made thirsty cars about as fashionable as narrow-leg pants. It was also enormously expensive, costing almost as much as Citroen’s grander DS. Just 847 were built before more conservative Peugeot took control of troubled Citroen and decided the rotary experiment wasn’t worth supporting. But the new bosses went further than merely axing the Birotor. Rather than keep supplying parts for a tiny population of troublesome cars, Citroen attempted to buy Birotors back and scrap them. Broad Arrow says roughly 250 are thought to survive today. This example formerly belonged to the Mullin Automotive Museum and shows an incredible 1,080 miles (1,740 km). But for Citroen geeks, this Monterey find gets even more tempting. Because Broad Arrow is also auctioning a 1970 M35 (see bottom two galleries), the road-going laboratory that preceded the Birotor. Its unusual Heuliez-built 2+2 body hides hydropneumatic suspension and a tiny 995 cc single-rotor Wankel. Citroen built only 267 M35s, loaning examples to selected customers who effectively became development drivers. It later bought back and destroyed many of those too. This Mullin Museum alumnus has covered 11,600 miles (18,704 km) and is estimated to fetch $30,000 to $40,000. So while collectors nearby fight over another million-dollar Porsche, you could conceivably spend around $50,000 and take home two incredibly rare survivors from one of Citroen’s wildest engineering dead ends.
